content.title: About
content.content: Macaroni or noodles with cheese is a ready‑to‑eat dish consisting of boiled pasta (or noodles) mixed with melted cheese, usually cheddar. It is popular as a quick lunch or snack, especially among children.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish originated in the United States in the early 1920s as an inexpensive, filling meal for workers.
In Russia, macaroni with cheese became widespread in the 1990s thanks to imported ready‑made packets.
There are many variations: with ham, broccoli, tomato sauce, or added spices.
Grated cheese is often browned separately to create a crispy crust.
The dish is a staple in school cafeterias and children's menus.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Cheese and pasta together provide a complete set of amino acids useful for growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cheese is rich in calcium, supporting bone and tooth health.

items.title: Energy supply
items.content: The dish quickly replenishes glucose stores, beneficial during physical activity.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Enriched pasta contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, aiding metabolism.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The combination of carbs and fats creates a lasting feeling of fullness.

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Creamy cheese makes the dish calorie‑dense; portion control is advised, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Lactose and milk protein
items.content: People with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy should use dairy‑free alternatives.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cheese often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: Traditional pasta contains gluten; gluten‑free versions are needed for celiac disease.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the dish hot, often topped with extra cheese or fresh herbs. You can add vegetables (broccoli, peas) or meat pieces for variety. Baking the mixture creates a golden crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared macaroni with cheese keeps in the refrigerator for 3‑4 days in an airtight container. Dry pasta should be stored in a cool, dry place, and grated cheese in its original packaging in the fridge.
